```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
```

```{r data}
library(survival)
vet <- survival::veteran
vet$trt <- factor(vet$trt, levels = 1:2, labels = c("standard", "test"))
fit <- coxph(Surv(time, status) ~ trt + karno + celltype + age, data = vet)
```

## 1. Scaled Schoenfeld residuals: `cox.zph()`

If $\beta_k$ is really $\beta_k(t)$, the scaled Schoenfeld residuals plus $\hat\beta_k$
track $\beta_k(t)$ (Grambsch & Therneau 1994). `cox.zph()` tests for a slope in time
(default time scale: the Kaplan–Meier transform).

```{r zph, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.5}
zp <- cox.zph(fit)
zp                                  # karno p = 0.0003, celltype p = 0.002
plot(zp[2], resid = TRUE, se = TRUE, lwd = 2)
abline(h = coef(fit)["karno"], col = "firebrick", lty = 2)
```

## 2. Graphical check: $\log\{-\log \hat S(t)\}$ against $\log t$

Under PH, $\log H(t \mid x) = \log H_0(t) + x^\top\beta$: the curves for groups are
parallel (vertical shift $\beta$).

```{r loglog, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.5}
vet$kgrp <- cut(vet$karno, c(0, 40, 60, 100), labels = c("10-40", "50-60", "70-99"))
km_k <- survfit(Surv(time, status) ~ kgrp, data = vet)
plot(km_k, fun = "cloglog", col = c("navy", "firebrick", "royalblue"), lwd = 2,
     xlab = "Days (log scale)", ylab = "log(-log S(t))")
legend("topleft", levels(vet$kgrp), col = c("navy", "firebrick", "royalblue"), lwd = 2, bty = "n")
```

## 3. Remedy A: stratify on Karnofsky group

Each stratum gets its own baseline hazard; no coefficient is estimated for karno.

```{r strata}
fit_s <- coxph(Surv(time, status) ~ trt + celltype + age + strata(kgrp), data = vet)
summary(fit_s)$coefficients
cox.zph(fit_s)
```

## 4. Remedy B: a time-varying coefficient (step function)

Split follow-up at 90 and 180 days and let karno have one coefficient per interval.

```{r step}
vs <- survSplit(Surv(time, status) ~ ., data = vet, cut = c(90, 180),
                episode = "tgroup", id = "id")
fit_t <- coxph(Surv(tstart, time, status) ~ trt + celltype + age + karno:strata(tgroup),
               data = vs)
round(summary(fit_t)$coefficients, 4)
cox.zph(fit_t)
AIC(fit, fit_t)        # same risk sets, so the partial likelihoods are comparable
```

## 5. Remedy C: a smooth time-varying coefficient with `tt()`

$\beta_{\text{karno}}(t) = a + b \log(t + 20)$.

```{r tt}
fit_tt <- coxph(Surv(time, status) ~ trt + celltype + age + karno + tt(karno), data = vet,
                tt = function(x, t, ...) x * log(t + 20))
b <- coef(fit_tt)
round(summary(fit_tt)$coefficients, 4)
sapply(c(30, 90, 180, 365), function(t) b["karno"] + b["tt(karno)"] * log(t + 20))
```

**Reading.** The Karnofsky score strongly predicts early deaths (coefficient about
$-0.048$ per point in the first 90 days, HR per 10 points $e^{-0.48} = 0.62$) but has
essentially no effect after 90 days. A single constant HR (0.72 per 10 points) averages
these two regimes. Cell type is also flagged by `cox.zph()`; stratifying on it as well
is a reasonable next step (exercise).
